capabilities: Convert whole notes, selections, or folders to speech via cloud or local TTS providers
Save generated audio in the vault and link it to the source note via an audio property
Play audio in a floating dock with speed control, seeking, and sentence highlighting
Align audio to note sentences locally using SenseVoice speech recognition timestamps
Batch-generate audio for folders on a daily schedule with incremental catch-up
extras: Desktop only (macOS tested; Windows and Linux untested this cycle). Pending Obsidian community directory review, so it must be installed manually or via BRAT. Cloud providers may charge fees; credentials are stored unencrypted in data.json and may be copied by vault sync. No voice models or reference audio are bundled with the local presets.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn notes into listenable audio or to follow playback against the note text.

relations.evidence: 安装并启用社区插件 BRAT
Providers include Volcengine, MiniMax, Replicate, a separately deployed GPT-SoVITS server, and custom HTTP endpoints.

requires.name: Cloud provider credentials (App ID / Access Token / API Key)
Separately deployed GPT-SoVITS server for local synthesis
Node.js, FFmpeg, sherpa-onnx-node, and a SenseVoice model for offline alignment

summary: Text-to-speech plugin that converts Markdown notes into audio files saved in the vault, plays them in a floating player, and highlights sentences during playback.
